title: Harell Data Debuts With $15M To Change Incentives, Speed Up AI Drug Discovery - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Harlan Robins, scientific founder of Adaptive Biotechnologies, has launched Bellevue-based Harell Data with $15M from Fuse and Cercano Management to build a cloud compute service for AI drug discovery that pays proprietary data generators a cut of revenue. The startup runs on CoreWeave/Nvidia infrastructure, is seeded with A-Alpha Bio and Adaptive datasets, and prices below AWS/Azure/Google Cloud.

insights.claim: AI model builders have hoovered up public data for free while the scientists who generated and curated it were never compensated, as with the Protein Data Bank curators who made AlphaFold possible.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Frames an emerging monetization gap that a data-rights business could arbitrage in life sciences.
insights.quote: This is just one of many examples in which AI model builders hoovered up public data for free and now are making their fortunes.

insights.claim: Harlan Robins argues that data used to train ML models is not being appropriately valued despite universal lip service, and that models like ChatGPT and Claude generate huge value from training on public data.
insights.speaker: Harlan Robins
insights.so_what: Underpins the entire premise that data generators deserve a revenue share, defining Harell's addressable wedge.
insights.quote: Data itself, especially for training ML models, isn’t getting appropriately valued.

insights.claim: Robins believes there must be a way for data generators to share in the value of discoveries made from their data, and founded Harell Data to build a more sustainable business for both data generators and AI model builders.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: The core mission that determines whether the company is a compute reseller or a novel data-rights marketplace.

insights.claim: Harell Data offers secure cloud computing through CoreWeave with industry-standard Nvidia GPUs, positioning itself as a specialized alternative to hyperscaler compute.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Reveals Harell is asset-light, reselling CoreWeave/Nvidia capacity rather than owning infrastructure.

insights.claim: Data providers who contribute curated datasets to Harell will receive a cut of the revenue Harell collects from AI model builders, paid upfront rather than as downstream royalties years later.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Upfront payment lowers adoption friction for data owners but shifts monetization risk onto Harell.

insights.claim: Harell intends to price its service to customers below what they currently pay big cloud providers Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Undercutting hyperscalers while paying data royalties implies thin margins unless curated data commands a premium.

insights.claim: Robins is not disclosing the percentage revenue cut offered to data generators but confirms they are paid upfront and will not chase downstream royalties on discoveries years after the fact.
insights.speaker: Harlan Robins
insights.so_what: Undisclosed economics make it hard to assess whether incentives are strong enough to attract quality data.

insights.claim: Harell Data has raised $15 million from Fuse, Cercano Management, and others to build its data-generator/AI-model-builder cloud service.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Seed-scale capital signals an early experiment rather than a proven model at scale.

insights.claim: Robins is the scientific founder of Seattle-based Adaptive Biotechnologies, a public company worth $3.9 billion, lending credibility to the new venture.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Founder track record de-risks the bet and eases access to proprietary datasets.

insights.claim: Harell, named as an amalgam of Harlan's first name and his 8-year-old son Ellis, has hired 11 people, none brought over from Adaptive where Robins remains a consultant.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A lean 11-person team confirms early stage and clean separation from Adaptive.

insights.claim: Harell's compute is initially populated with two proprietary datasets: A-Alpha Bio's protein-protein binding affinity data and Adaptive's T cell receptor binding data.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Quality of these anchor datasets will determine whether AI drug-discovery customers show up.

insights.claim: Robins contends much valuable industry data lives in silos inaccessible to AI model builders, and unlocking it via shared prosperity could accelerate medical discovery.
insights.speaker: Harlan Robins
insights.so_what: The bet that better incentives free up siloed data is the mechanism meant to speed drug discovery.

insights.claim: Robins pitched the revenue-sharing idea to big cloud companies, offering to drive hundreds of millions in revenue if they shared a cut with data generators, but those talks went nowhere.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Incumbent rejection is why the opportunity exists for an independent player like Harell.

insights.claim: Robins says hyperscalers declined because they are supply-limited, not customer-limited, already selling every bit of compute they get.
insights.speaker: Harlan Robins
insights.so_what: In a GPU-constrained market, incumbents have no incentive to share revenue, leaving room for differentiated data-plus-compute offerings.
insights.quote: They are selling every bit of compute they are getting already. They are supply limited, not limited on customers.

insights.claim: Harell's viability is unproven and depends on simultaneously appealing to AI drug-discovery customers and fairly compensating data providers, with Robins about to get real-world market feedback.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Two-sided marketplace risk means Harell must clear both demand and supply hurdles to survive.
insights.quote: The only way to find out is to try a different business model.
